A 82-year-old woman with chronic idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) visits her hematologist for
routine follow-up. She has been receiving long-term corticosteroids for ITP and has undergone multiple
treatments with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) and rituximab. Laboratory results show a white
blood cell count of 8, hematocrit of 35, and platelet count of 14. Due to refractory ITP and persistent
thrombocytopenia, her hematologist recommends splenectomy. What is the appropriate timing for
vaccination against encapsulated organisms and the initiation of penicillin prophylaxis for this patient?
Answer Choices: (A) Vaccinate: 2 weeks prior to surgery; Penicillin: 1 week post-surgery for 5 years (B)
Vaccinate: 2 weeks prior to surgery; Penicillin: at time of surgery for an indefinite course (C) Vaccinate:
at the time of surgery; Penicillin: 2 weeks prior to surgery for an indefinite course (D) Vaccinate: 1 week
prior to surgery; Penicillin: at time of surgery for 2 years (E) Vaccinate: 2 weeks after surgery; Penicillin:
2 weeks post-surgery for an indefinite course (F) Vaccinate: 2 weeks prior to surgery; Penicillin: 2
weeks post-surgery for 5 years (G) Vaccinate: 2 weeks prior to surgery; Penicillin: at time of surgery for
5 years (H) Vaccinate: 4 weeks prior to surgery; Penicillin: at time of surgery for 1 year (I) Vaccinate: 1
week prior to surgery; Penicillin: at time of surgery for an indefinite course (J) Vaccinate: 4 weeks prior
to surgery; Penicillin: 1 week post-surgery for an indefinite course
 A. Vaccinate: 2 weeks prior to surgery; Penicillin: 1 week post-surgery for 5 years
B. Vaccinate: 2 weeks after surgery; Penicillin: 2 weeks post-surgery for an indefinite course
C. Vaccinate: 1 week prior to surgery; Penicillin: at time of surgery for 2 years
D. Vaccinate: 2 weeks prior to surgery; Penicillin: at time of surgery for an indefinite course

E. Vaccinate: 4 weeks prior to surgery; Penicillin: 1 week post-surgery for an indefinite course
F. Vaccinate: 1 week prior to surgery; Penicillin: at time of surgery for an indefinite course
G. Vaccinate: at the time of surgery; Penicillin: 2 weeks prior to surgery for an indefinite course
H. Vaccinate: 2 weeks prior to surgery; Penicillin: at time of surgery for 5 years
I. Vaccinate: 4 weeks prior to surgery; Penicillin: at time of surgery for 1 year
J. Vaccinate: 2 weeks prior to surgery; Penicillin: 2 weeks post-surgery for 5 years
